title: Anybody working besides Three.js stack?
author: StudyInProgress
selftext: Every post here is about Three.js stack. Anybody is using other stack to build game with AI. I'm new to game dev

comments.author: count023
comments.body: unity and godot are the two other major common ones being used right now.

replies.author: QuestHouseGM
replies.body: I have a little hobby project I use Godot for. Claude hooks right into Godot and Blender, and it lets me know when I have something to look at. Couldn’t be easier.

replies.author: OMBERX
replies.body: How do you hook up Claude into Godot personally?

replies.author: QuestHouseGM
replies.body: You just tell Claude to use it. Even if it isn’t installed yet, Claude will install for you too.

replies.author: OMBERX
replies.body: I've been working in Godot for years.  I'm just very new and ignorant to a lot of AI tools.  I use browser ChatGPT very sparingly and that's about it.  I would like to give Claude the context of all the games and prototypes I already have and just have it help me write some scripts.  How would I go about setting all of that up?  Is there a free plan for doing that?

replies.author: QuestHouseGM
replies.body: I feel you! So you’re going to want to do this in Claude Code specifically. Open a chat in Claude code, give it the filepath to your main folders where things are, and describe to it what’s in there in the chat. Ask it to go through and understand everything and report back to you with questions. Sonnet or Opus should be fine for this.

comments.author: siberianmi
comments.body: I’m using Godot.  Three is popular because agents often reach for it to one shot things I think.

replies.author: StudyInProgress
replies.body: Yeah. I feel Three.js are good for demo. But for actual game, game engines are better choice. What's your workflow with AI?

replies.author: siberianmi
replies.body:
Same for game development as it is for my day job.  Have a conversation with it to reach a shared understanding of what I want built, break out into issues that are small and have clear outcomes.  Fire up a series of new agents to work them one by one.

I am having fun with doing game assets with AI iteratively [on my phone](https://pixelsbyproxy.substack.com/p/my-art-department-is-a-python-script).   It’s helping me doom scroll less.

I’m building a voxel based isometric shooter loosely based on an old c64 game I remember playing a ton - reimagined as a more modern title.  So it’s just a nostalgia trip at the moment.

https://preview.redd.it/mox8hk86f1th1.jpeg?width=3840&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=6013212861185b574a014fcaa85c2aad3386036e

comments.author: Rsouss
comments.body: Babylon is much more advanced. I'm using it to create an engine.

comments.author: Gigaslavx
comments.body:
Web is a joke. You can rush an ok demo but that's it can't grow and you learn nothing

Unity is probably best balance. Godot is simple and easy, and unreal overkill

Just know what you doing have expertise and experience don't blindly rely on ai use it as a tool. As a beginner perhaps Godot is better at least compared to web but yeah be realistic in regard to expectations 

I say work on fun game concept instead of overthinking small bits blender etc 

But yeah ensure you build foundation in clear layers and right order or it will be like web slop all tangled together

replies.author: joeyismusic
replies.body: You can build everything in three.js and then grab a codex Astra or Claude fable session and create a port to anything else in a few days. Currently doing that myself to a game I spent months making - porting to monogame c#.

replies.author: Gigaslavx
replies.body:
Yeah that's fair but I rather use proper engine from beginning

I think web is great to test proto types it's so quick, sure it's like rough angles but you get general gist if it's fun or not

Yeah engine takes time to set up I mean build layers but it pays off

So I say spend a few days if needed quick demo web see for yourself what you think best direction then start slowly building on proper engine

replies.author: joeyismusic
replies.body: Just depends on how you like to work. The rapid iteration speed of web workflow is still faster than just about anything else.

comments.author: saumanahaii
comments.body: I use Godot and it works pretty well.  I do web exports too.

comments.author: JessenReinhart
comments.body: me, im using Phaser. [civ-strategy.vercel.app](http://civ-strategy.vercel.app) GitHub Repo here: [Repo](https://github.com/JessenReinhart/CivStrategy)

comments.author: _OVERHATE_
comments.body: Ai games are not meant to be played by an audience larger than 1, so three.js is more than enough. Everything else is overkill

comments.author: TheMarasligil
comments.body: Flutter for mobile games, godot for PC games to be honest. I feel like these are mostly enough for non-3d games.

replies.author: TheMarasligil
replies.body: Neither was i, but for the last 3 published games i was able to have flutter purr like a kittie with all sdks we had

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
anything works to be honest. you can have AI make a game running in the terminal with ASCII graphics if you want.

threejs is good because 1) AIs prefer javascript 2) pretty good 3d rendering capability for a free library 3) works on browsers just fine

since AI is involved, the only concern is really just the target environment i.e. do you want your game to run on PCs? phone? browser-only?

comments.author: shuozhe
comments.body:
Unity. Native C with sdl mostly. For work also random tools that is based on older unreal.

Using web only for prototyping, once project get bigger, even all the flagship model struggles :(

comments.author: advator
comments.body: Using mcp blender and unreal. I'm a unity user but mcp works better on unreal

comments.author: KalElReturns89
comments.body: I've used Godot and Unreal with AI in successful projects. Unity I've seen works great as well.
